Damn, you really nailed them to the wall at 1:19:00 with "Frame not analyzed for stabilization; click Analyze."   The media-mancy section really hits close to home for me, though. I grew up with a parent who was a pretty hardcore conspiracy theorist, to the extent that I recognized every diagram and fringe idea you brought up in this video. They got me into identifying "important" numbers and symbols in movies, TV, news segments, presidential speeches, etc. at a young age, and we used to make a game out of pointing them out in the media we watched together. I decided pretty early on that I didn't believe any of it, I'm thankful for that every day, but hearing about it constantly growing up means I still subconsciously notice those same "signs" and "synchronicities" in media. Something you touch on in this video and when discussing Megan Phelps-Roper in your "Witch Trials of..." video is that a lot of people raised in cult-like religions have a tendency to embrace conspiracism once they leave, not only because these institutions operate in fundamentally similar ways, but because (as Megan even puts it) abandoning a fundamentalist religion forces you to question your ability to perceive reality. I think a lot of people who have been raised with a strong religious foundation, one that establishes the very fabric of the universe and reality as divine and intentional, find that leaving their religion also leaves holes in their concept of reality. They may not be able to entirely abandon the logic and language of the religion in which they were raised, so intentionalist conspiracies, patriarchal power structures, "signs" and hidden meanings and divination all slot into the fractured remnants of their abandoned worldview.  Thankfully my parent is no longer engaged in *the conspiracies of today*, and has actually been making incredible progress over the years that I'm very proud of them for. Oddly, aside from finding out they had queer children, one of the things that moved them away from far-right conspiracies was the Q-Anon movement itself. Early on I heard them express a lot of frustration that Q followers were, "Interpreting the signs wrong," that they were amateurs and didn't know what they were talking about, which I think led to some difficult introspection about their own beliefs.  Thank you for this video, it was honestly very cathartic.
